program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-entry deep passes; consolidate and validate once after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Public PubMed/PMC abstracts and ordinary web research
manual clinical-identity, route, formulation, population, biomarker, evidence-quality and safety calibration

policy.validation_strategy: deep source calibration per pass; expensive repository-wide validation after Wave 2500

waves.title: Live biotherapeutics and nutraceuticals: Exploring the differences and synergies.
waves.population: regulatory, mechanistic, animal, and human evidence across live biotherapeutic products and nutraceuticals
waves.finding: The review distinguishes live biotherapeutic products from nutraceuticals by product definition, regulation, biological standardization, and evidence expectations while describing potential combination strategies.
waves.safety: Useful taxonomy and evidence-framework context, but it does not establish clinical efficacy for a specific product or indication.

waves.title: Ginseng Polysaccharides: A Comprehensive Review of Extraction, Structure, In Vivo Fate, Health-Promoting Functions, and Application Potential.
waves.population: preclinical, pharmacokinetic, and limited translational literature on ginseng polysaccharides
waves.finding: Ginseng polysaccharides show immunomodulatory, metabolic, antioxidant, and gut-related activities across experimental models, with biological effects strongly influenced by extraction and structural characteristics.
waves.safety: Clinical efficacy, standardized exposure, and human dose-response remain insufficiently established.

waves.title: Factors influencing the effect of melatonin on sleep quality in children with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: children with autism spectrum disorder and sleep disturbance
waves.finding: Melatonin improved pooled sleep-quality and total-sleep-time outcomes in children with autism, with heterogeneity across formulations, durations, and trial characteristics.
waves.safety: Pediatric ASD evidence is population-specific; meta-regression dose estimates are exploratory and must not be converted into dosing guidance.

waves.title: Does Crocus sativus (Saffron) Have an Influence or Effect on Ocular Health: A Systematic Literature Review.
waves.population: patients across AMD, glaucoma, diabetic macular edema, central serous retinopathy, Stargardt disease, and pediatric myopia
waves.finding: Clinical trials reported favorable visual or retinal outcomes with saffron, crocin, or crocetin in several ocular conditions, but indications, preparations, doses, and endpoints were heterogeneous.
waves.safety: Positive results across heterogeneous eye diseases and preparations cannot be treated as one generalized saffron eye-health effect.

waves.title: Prebiotics/synbiotics as natural alternatives for brain development and aging - focus on nutrigenomic and direct effects: a systematic review.
waves.population: mixed developmental, aging, animal, mechanistic, and limited human literature
waves.finding: Prebiotic and synbiotic interventions show plausible gut-brain, inflammatory, metabolic, and nutrigenomic effects relevant to brain development and aging, but much of the evidence remains mechanistic or preclinical.
waves.safety: Human cognitive or neurodevelopmental efficacy is not established across products or life stages.

waves.title: Effects of Curcumin/Turmeric Supplementation on Lipid Profile in Subjects With Prediabetes and Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: people with prediabetes or diabetes
waves.finding: Curcumin/turmeric modestly reduced triglycerides, total cholesterol, and LDL-C and modestly increased HDL-C in pooled trials, but heterogeneity exceeded 80% and GRADE certainty was low.
waves.safety: Low-certainty, highly heterogeneous evidence should not be converted into product-equivalent lipid-lowering claims.

waves.title: Gut microbiota, probiotics, and migraine: a clinical review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: clinical systematic review with meta-analysis of probiotic RCTs
waves.population: people with migraine
waves.finding: The small probiotic trial subset suggested reduced migraine frequency, while pooled severity and duration outcomes were not significantly improved and heterogeneity was high.
waves.safety: Only a small number of probiotic trials contributed to pooled results; strain-specific efficacy remains uncertain.

waves.title: Effects of creatine supplementation on muscle strength gains-a meta-analysis and systematic review.
waves.population: adults in strength-training and exercise studies
waves.finding: Creatine supplementation produced a small-to-moderate pooled improvement in strength, with larger effects in some untrained and resistance-training subgroups.
waves.safety: Moderator and dose subgroup findings are exploratory and do not establish a single optimal intake regimen.

waves.title: Probiotics and Synbiotics Supplementation Reduce Inflammatory Cytokines in Individuals with Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Findings from a Systematic Review Meta-analysis.
waves.population: 1,321 adults with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes
waves.finding: Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation modestly reduced CRP, IL-6, and TNF-alpha in pooled trials.
waves.safety: These are biomarker endpoints across heterogeneous strains and synbiotic formulations and do not by themselves establish clinical outcome benefit.

waves.title: Modulating the gut microbiome to enhance cancer immunotherapy: a systematic review and Meta-Analysis of probiotics and FMT as adjuncts.
waves.population: 3,274 patients receiving cancer immunotherapy
waves.finding: Microbiome-directed interventions, including probiotics and fecal microbiota transplantation, were associated with improved progression-free and overall survival in pooled analyses, but the evidence mixed intervention types and nonrandomized designs.
waves.safety: Observational confounding, combination therapy, cancer type, microbiome intervention, and treatment regimen prevent causal probiotic efficacy claims.

waves.title: Effectiveness of green tea (Camellia sinensis) based mouth rinse on oral health status, pain and quality of life among advanced head and neck cancer patients in a tertiary care centre-a randomized controlled trial.
waves.population: 64 patients with advanced head-and-neck cancer receiving palliative care
waves.finding: A green-tea-based mouth rinse improved selected oral-health, pain, and quality-of-life measures compared with control care.
waves.safety: This is topical supportive-care evidence in advanced cancer and cannot support systemic green-tea supplement claims.

waves.title: Does inflammation moderate the effect of vitamin D supplementation on depressive symptoms? Results of an interventional study in children and adolescents.
waves.study: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled vitamin-D intervention
waves.population: 92 vitamin-D-deficient children/adolescents with depressive symptoms
waves.finding: Vitamin D supplementation did not show a consistent antidepressant effect across the parent trial's outcomes, and baseline inflammation did not reliably identify a treatment-responsive subgroup.
waves.safety: Small secondary analysis in deficient youths; exploratory inflammatory moderation should not be used for treatment selection.

waves.title: Ginger in supportive therapy against side effects of oncological treatment: a systematic review.
waves.population: 2,409 oncology patients across chemotherapy/radiotherapy supportive-care studies
waves.finding: Ginger showed mixed signals for nausea/vomiting, xerostomia, nutrition, fatigue, and quality of life; several outcomes were positive, several were null, and some trials suggested disadvantages for nausea/vomiting.
waves.safety: Formulations, doses, cancer treatments, and endpoints varied widely; the evidence does not support a broad anti-side-effect claim.

waves.title: Oral ferrous sulphate supplementation has greater efficacy, but lower tolerance than iron (III)-hydroxide polymaltose complexes in exercising women with low iron stores.
waves.population: 57 exercising women with low iron stores completing follow-up
waves.finding: Ferrous sulfate increased ferritin much more than iron-polymaltose complex, while the polymaltose formulation produced fewer gastrointestinal symptoms.
waves.safety: Direct efficacy-tolerability tradeoff between formulations; findings apply to iron-deficient exercising women rather than iron-replete populations.

waves.title: Vitamin D Status and Supplementation in Lumbar Spinal Fusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Radiographic and Clinical Outcomes.
waves.population: patients undergoing lumbar spinal fusion
waves.finding: Vitamin-D supplementation/status was associated with higher fusion success and lower fusion failure in pooled radiographic outcomes, while patient-reported outcome differences were inconsistent and often below minimal clinically important thresholds.
waves.safety: Surgical-population evidence is heterogeneous and should not be generalized to routine musculoskeletal supplementation.

waves.title: Effect of calcium supplementation in pregnancy on maternal anemia and iron status: secondary analyses of two randomized trials in India and Tanzania.
waves.study: secondary analyses of two large randomized trials
waves.population: pregnant women in India and Tanzania receiving iron-folic acid plus different calcium doses
waves.finding: Higher versus lower calcium supplementation did not meaningfully worsen hemoglobin, anemia, or iron-status outcomes when both groups also received iron-folic acid.
waves.safety: This is a pregnancy dose-comparison context with concomitant iron-folic acid and does not establish general calcium-iron interaction rules.

waves.title: Morin: A Comprehensive Review of Its Sources, Nutraceutical Prospects, Chemistry, and Pharmacological Insights.
waves.population: chemical, preclinical, pharmacokinetic, and limited translational literature
waves.finding: Morin shows antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, metabolic, and other pharmacologic activities in experimental systems, but poor bioavailability and sparse human evidence limit translation.
waves.safety: Clinical efficacy, formulation equivalence, chronic safety, and human dose-response remain unestablished.

waves.title: Zinc-L-carnosine mouthwash in oral mucositis patients: a single-blind, randomized, controlled trial.
waves.population: 42 patients with oral mucositis
waves.finding: Zinc-L-carnosine mouthwash reduced mucositis severity, symptoms, and analgesic use compared with control.
waves.safety: This is a topical mouthwash formulation and does not validate systemic zinc or carnosine supplementation for mucositis.

waves.title: Panax ginseng C.A. Mey. as Multi-Target Regulators of Vascular Homeostasis: Pharmacological Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
waves.population: predominantly cell and animal vascular literature with limited human context
waves.finding: Ginseng constituents influence endothelial, inflammatory, oxidative, nitric-oxide, and vascular-signaling pathways in preclinical models.
waves.safety: Many experimental concentrations exceed plausible plasma exposure after oral use; human vascular efficacy remains hypothesis-generating.

waves.title: Effect of melatonin as an adjunct to non-surgical periodontal therapy in the treatment of periodontitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of adjunctive clinical trials
waves.population: patients receiving nonsurgical periodontal therapy
waves.finding: Adjunctive melatonin improved probing-depth and selected attachment outcomes compared with periodontal therapy alone, with heterogeneity and limited follow-up.
waves.safety: Benefit was measured as an adjunct to standard periodontal therapy and cannot establish stand-alone melatonin efficacy.

waves.title: Can coenzyme Q10 supplementation reduce exercise-induced muscle damage and oxidative stress in athletes? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 440 athletes or physically active participants
waves.finding: CoQ10 reduced pooled malondialdehyde, LDH, and creatine-kinase responses after exercise, while total antioxidant capacity was not significantly improved.
waves.safety: Evidence certainty was low to very low and endpoints were biomarkers rather than performance, recovery time, or clinical injury.

waves.title: Nutritional interventions and dietary supplements in muscle diseases: a systematic review.
waves.population: patients across inflammatory myopathies, muscular dystrophies, metabolic myopathies, and other muscle diseases
waves.finding: Nutrition and supplement effects were highly disease-specific; creatine plus exercise showed benefit in some inflammatory myopathy contexts, while high-dose creatine worsened outcomes in McArdle disease and many interventions had insufficient evidence.
waves.safety: Cross-disease pooling would be unsafe; both benefit and condition-specific harm must remain explicit.

waves.title: Effects of probiotic and metformin co-administration versus metformin monotherapy on anthropometric measurements, hormones, and glucolipid profile in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: women with PCOS receiving metformin
waves.finding: Adding probiotics to metformin modestly improved HOMA-IR and showed borderline hormonal effects while reducing some metformin-associated gastrointestinal adverse effects.
waves.safety: Combination therapy prevents attribution to probiotics alone and trials were short and heterogeneous.

waves.title: Effectiveness of probiotic supplements on cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: 994 participants with mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer's disease
waves.finding: Probiotics modestly improved pooled cognitive outcomes, but effect size varied by disease, strain/product, and trial duration; the synthesis overlaps with smaller probiotic-cognition meta-analyses.
waves.safety: Overlapping evidence, strain heterogeneity, and subgroup dose/duration signals should not be promoted as a universal regimen.

waves.title: Effects of Caffeine Dose and Administration Method on Time-Trial Performance: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: 612 participants completing exercise time trials
waves.finding: Caffeine improved time-trial performance across several delivery strategies; low-dose capsules, moderate-dose capsules, and caffeinated gum ranked among the better-performing approaches.
waves.safety: Network rankings and dose categories do not define a universally optimal or safe dose because individual response and sport context vary.
